title: Ordinary affine-line homotopy invariance for finite twists
statement:
Fix the finite datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$ for $n\geq1$, and the twists $A(r)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with their finite small-etale realizations of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].  Let $X$ be an arbitrary $k$-scheme and let $p:\mathbf A^1_X\to X$ be the affine-line projection of [def-sbc-affine-space] (relative dimension one).  Use ordinary sheaf cohomology [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (zero in negative degrees for a sheaf) on the small sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-derived-direct-image] in the respective topologies. For every integer $r$, the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]
$$
 A(r)_X\longrightarrow Rp_*A(r)_{\mathbf A^1_X}
$$
is an isomorphism on the small etale site and on the small pro-etale site (for the etale-origin finite twist).  Consequently, for every integer $q$, pullback $p^*:H^q(X,A(r))\to H^q(\mathbf A^1_X,A(r))$ is an isomorphism in either topology.  These isomorphisms are natural in $X$ and in finite coefficient maps, and the etale and pro-etale isomorphisms are identified by the canonical comparison.

source.place: Clause (a), Reduction to a geometric fibre, and Coefficients: arbitrary-base and all-twists refinement of the ordinary affine-line acyclicity input, needed in the shear paragraph of main-20261015/sk-prop-an/lem-pur-frame-independence.proof.md. This new statement is agent-formulated; the unit itself states the finite-type case.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-finite-twist-root-trivialization], $A$ is finite with $\ell$-power order, $\ell^nA=0$, and a common primitive root trivializes every signed twist in both sites, compatibly with pullback, coefficient maps and site comparison. It suffices to test the canonical etale unit on the constant module $A$.

By [def-sbc-affine-space], over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ the projection is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence affine and qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. For each geometric point put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$, a strictly henselian local $k$-scheme. Apply [lem-pur-strict-local-smooth-transfer] to obtain $R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_k,A)\cong R\Gamma(\mathbf A^1_S,A)$ by pullback preserving constants. By [lem-pur-affine-line-finite-group-devissage], the first complex is $A[0]$ via constants. Thus the constants hypothesis of [lem-pur-strict-local-constant-unit-criterion] holds at every point; that criterion proves the canonical unit for $A$ invertible in the fixed-ring module category.

source.place: Reduction to a geometric fibre and Degrees 0 and 1

proof.text: Conjugate by the compatible sheaf isomorphisms of step 1. Naturality of the adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] identifies the resulting map with $A(r)_X\to Rp_*A(r)_{\mathbf A^1_X}$, so it is invertible. Apply [lem-pur-ordinary-unit-site-sections-transport] to the qcqs $p$ and the degree-zero finite etale twist: it gives the actual pro-etale unit, both ordinary cohomology pullbacks in every degree, and equality of these maps under the canonical site comparison. The finite pro-etale coefficient object is the prescribed twist by step 1.

Apply [lem-pur-ordinary-unit-exchange-naturality] to any base map $v:X'\to X$ and any finite coefficient map. Its unit equation gives naturality of the derived isomorphisms, its pullback equations give naturality of their cohomology maps, and its comparison clause identifies these equations on the two sites. Both units are invertible by steps 2 and 3, so exchange is invertible on these coefficients and the inverse isomorphisms satisfy the same naturality squares. Negative degrees and the empty base are included in the cited criteria. No chosen primitive root enters the definition of these canonical maps.
